---
title: "Homework: Room Adventure...Revolutions"
---

The starting version of the game has two rooms and two unimplemented handlers. Your task is to implement those handlers, expand the mansion into four rooms, and make 2 significant additions to the game.

## 0. Implement the Base Game (5 pts)

You should have the base game implemented at this point. If not, just follow the instructions on the previous pages in this activity.

## 1. Implement `handleLook` (5 pts)

The `handleLook` method should search the current room's items. If the noun matches an item, it sets `status` to that item's description.

::: {.callout-note}
## Details: Implement `handleLook`

Replace the empty `handleLook` stub. The method should:

1. Set `status` to a default message of `"I don't see that item."`
2. Loop through `currentRoom.items`.
3. Set `status` to corresponding `itemDescription`.

Remember to use `.equals()` for string comparison. `items` and `itemDescriptions` are parallel arrays, so index `i` in one corresponds to index `i` in the other.
:::



## 2. Implement `handleTake` (5 pts)

The `handleTake` method should search the current room's lootables. If the noun matches one, it should move that item into the player's inventory and remove it from the room.

Since `inventory` is a fixed-size array of 5 slots, you need to find the first `null` slot before placing the item.

::: {.callout-note}
## Challenge: Implement `handleTake`

Replace the empty `handleTake` stub. The method should:

1. Set `status` to a default message of `"I don't see that item."`
2. Loop through `currentRoom.lootables`.
3. If it finds the `lootable` in the `currentRoom`:
   - Place it in the first blank inventory slot
   - Set `status` to `"Looted."`

**Note:** Compare to `null` with `==`. The `.equals()` rule only applies when comparing two string values to each other.
:::



## 3. Add Rooms 3 and 4 and Populate them (5 pts)

Update `setupGame` to create two more rooms. Arrange them in the same square layout used in the previous Room Adventure activity:

- **Room 3**: south of Room 1, east leads to Room 4
- **Room 4**: south of Room 2, west leads to Room 3

You will also need to make updates to Room 1 and Room 2 in order to connect them to Room 3 and Room 4. 

Be sure to populate Room 3 and Room 4 with items and lootables.


## 4. Make Two Significant Additions to the Game (10 pts each)

Now make the game your own game by making two significant additions to the game. Note that additing any number of additional rooms can only be counted as 1 of your two additions.

Here are some ideas on what you can add. Do not limit yourself to these ideas.

- More Rooms and Items (this can only count as one feature, regardless of the number of rooms and items you add)
- An additional piece of functionality (i.e. a "use" command or an "eat" command). Each piece of functionality can count as a separate additional feature.
- Making Improvements to the Code (ex: using Hashmaps or classes to represent the Items/Exits/etc).
- For this, the program may function the same, but you improve the codebase.
- Anything else you dream up.

## Other (5 pts)

Here are some other things to be mindful of for your submission.

- Be sure to turn in a `README.md` file with your submission that outlines the additions you made (you can turn in a `.zip` that includes both.)
- Be sure to include you name in both the `RoomAdventure.java` file and the `README.md` file.
- Be sure to turn in the source code (the `.java` file). Your prof will compile it on their machine.
- Be sure to use good coding etiquette such as comments, descriptive variable names, indentation, and other aspects that make code easy to read.
